fields.identity: - A mysterious tattoo shop that grants supernatural abilities through tattoos. A GENUINELY benevolent anomalous place, "a single ray of light in the dark" in a world where every other bargain costs body, soul, or at minimum conscience.
fields.location: - The shop is mobile, appearing in different anomalies and locations. Usually Appears in underground parking-lot areas as a cramped commercial space next to the parking lot. Translucent glass door with an automatic opening button, shop sign in elaborate calligraphic script at the corner of the door. After leaving, the space becomes truly vacant again.
fields.environment:
- Interior is clean, professionally maintained despite appearing somewhat shabby. Counter area where the operator sits. Walls display service notices and menu boards.
- LED panel in the ceiling centre showing the moon, casting artificial moonlight downward. Treatment chair positioned under artificial moonlight.
fields.rules:
##### Service flow
- Only one customer receives treatment at a time.
- Operator provides a lemon beverage and a design catalogue. Each design carries a power, legible partly through its imagery (one example: a rough, lyrical pen-stroke tree bearing a single red tomato, associated with COURAGE).
- Catalogue tier varies based on payment quality (from Basic 3 up to Royal Special Premium 1).
- Customer selects design or requests the operator's recommendation based on desired traits. Operator may provide additional complimentary services (e.g., aromatherapy massage).
- Customer sits in the central chair under moonlight. Operator wears steampunk-style goggles and operates the large tattoo machine. Moonlight is drawn into the machine and focused at the needle tip.
- The tattoos themselves vanish the next day, but the abilities they depict are absorbed into the recipient and remain permanent.

##### Currency
- Payment method: barter only — no cash accepted.
- Preferred items: items related to the sea.
fields.keeper:
##### The Tattooist
- A not-human artist with gleaming, attentive eyes and impeccable warmth. Female-presenting individual with curly hair tied back tightly, dense Korean-script tattoos covering the neck. Sleeveless clothing.
- Speaks not at all; all communication runs through pre-written booklets and wall notices.

fields.location:
- A small, serene shop standing under what is always described as a clear night sky: crescent moon, a rare scatter of visible stars. Vertical signboard. The glass door is aged to a slight cloudiness but polished to a shine, and hung with a metal-bookmark wind chime.
- Warm, well-maintained interior with soft lighting, aged wooden shelves, a counter-style desk, and new/antique books arranged in irregular but deliberate order.
- A bead curtain separates the public shopfront from the owner’s shadowed back area.
fields.rules:
##### Nature and Function
- One of the Supernatural Disaster Management Bureau's standing sources for numinous artifacts, and its oldest: the cooperative relationship dates to the late Joseon period and has never lapsed.
- Known property of the premises: talisman-crafting performed here imposes a markedly reduced karmic cost on the maker. the house absorbs, deflects, or simply declines to charge the usual price of such work. The owner's assistance is available besides.
- Repair and purification are house services: artifacts are restored by fire poured gently INTO them, old cracks burning away "like grime scrubbed off", the object's dignity explicitly minded throughout.
- Prices are not fixed; payment depends on the buyer’s identity, the requested item’s value, and the nature of the transaction. Accepted payment may include cash, gold, equivalent objects, labour/services, other books as trade-ins, or unusual “book-form” substitutes. Custom services can also be negotiated as part of the transaction.
fields.keeper:
##### The Owner
- An entity of unknown nature who remains behind the bead curtain in the shadowed back area. Only the owner’s right hand is normally visible, emerging from behind the curtain to write notes, receive payment, or pass objects across the counter. Communicates through neat, formal script written by hand.
- Shows polite bewilderment at unusual payment methods but remains flexible if the offered item can be interpreted as equivalent value.
fields.access:
##### Access and Etiquette
- When the lights are ON: safe to enter. Human customers and ordinary transactions are permitted.
- When the lights are OFF: DO NOT ENTER. A non-human or supernatural entity is conducting business.
- House etiquette is implicit but firm: goods are guests; treat them accordingly.
- Communication with the owner is conducted only through written notes. Do not attempt to look behind the bead curtain.

fields.identity: The Dokkaebi Workshop is a traditional Korean workshop where dokkaebis gather after nightfall to drink, eat buckwheat rice cakes, and craft anomalous items. Most depart before morning, but a few commonly remain behind during the day. Visitors who approach them respectfully and bring suitable gifts may commission repairs or custom-made objects.
fields.access:
- The Workshop has no permanent address. It appears without warning inside an ordinary residential district, usually occupying an empty lot, a dead-end alley, or a space between houses where no building previously stood. Nearby residents rarely notice the change and may behave as though the hanok has always been there.
- Its entrance can be reached normally once it has appeared, though visitors who leave the area may be unable to find the same route again. The Workshop remains until the following dawn or morning, then disappears without leaving structural damage or an empty foundation behind. Any surrounding streets, walls, or buildings displaced by its presence return to their original arrangement.
- The same Workshop may reappear elsewhere, but no reliable method of predicting or forcing its arrival is known.
fields.location:
- The Workshop takes the form of a traditional hanok courtyard surrounded by wooden buildings with tiled roofs and ivory-colored plaster walls. The main building contains the forge and work area, while smaller rooms are used for storage, drinking, and meals.
- Although the courtyard is open to the sky, the air inside is completely still. Smoke rises vertically, hanging cloth does not move, and sounds from the surrounding neighborhood become distant once the entrance is crossed. During the day, the grounds are quiet enough to feel abandoned, even when one or more dokkaebis remain inside working.
- The stillness and traditional architecture sharply separate the Workshop from the modern residential streets outside it.
fields.rules:
##### Nature and Function
- The day-loitering dokkaebi will, if brought good things and asked nicely, craft items with genuine delight: the workshop functions as an artisan forge for the anomalous.
- Commissioning involves the client WISHING, aloud and sincerely, what the object should become. the wish is part of the manufacturing process, not a pleasantry.
- The Workshop can also repair damaged anomalous objects, though a dokkaebi may refuse an item it considers boring, offensive, or beyond saving.
- Workshop goods are traceable after sale: the workshop can track its products, down to whether an item's numinous charge has been spent. Theft, resale, and misrepresentation are therefore poor life choices.

##### Visitor Protocol
- Visitors should address the dokkaebis as "elder" and maintain a polite, humble manner throughout the exchange. Appropriate gifts should be presented before discussing work, with alcohol, food, unusual materials, and entertaining objects generally receiving favorable reactions.
- Requests should be phrased as wishes rather than demands. Greed, impatience, or attempts to negotiate after an agreement has been accepted may cause the commission to be refused or deliberately interpreted in the least favorable way possible.
- Dokkaebis frequently propose alternative designs or additional features of their own. Their recommendations should be heard respectfully, even when declined.
fields.keeper:
##### Dokkaebi
- The Workshop's dokkaebis are large, broad-built figures recognizable by their loud voices and distinctive hair ribbons styled after traditional daenggi. Their speech combines archaic Korean expressions with modern vocabulary, often shifting between the two without warning.
- They are playful, mischievous, and fond of pranks, but show sincere pride in their craftsmanship. They become especially cheerful when presented with an unusual problem or a request they have never attempted before.
- Most are fond of alcohol and communal drinking. Their hospitality can be generous, but visitors should not mistake friendliness for harmlessness. A dokkaebi insulted in its own Workshop may treat retaliation as another form of amusement.

fields.location:
##### Location
A small special zone derived from a tale; the anonymous bazaar of the entire abnormal world. There is no address, because the address is every manhole.
fields.access:
- Access rides on its parent tale, 'The Manhole's Arm'. an arm that travels between the living world and the afterworld through manholes, luring people close with an object held invitingly in its palm, to eat them. Those who know the Market exploit the same passage by approaching the lure as either a seller or a buyer.
- The market's founding insight: insert only your arm into a anomalous manholes occupied by the Manhole Arms phenomenon., and you join the lure's side of the transaction. A seller holds an item and inserts that hand into a manhole occupied by the phenomenon. The item disappears from their real hand, while a COPY of the arm appears from a wall inside the Market, holding the item in the same position. The seller's actual arm remains attached and unharmed. 
- A visitor inserts an empty hand into the manhole. With no item to register, the passage draws the visitor's entire body into the Market's exhibition space. An empty hand allows its owner to enter as a customer.
fields.environment:
- The Faceless Market is a dark, damp exhibition space with shallow liquid pooled across the floor and minimal lighting.
- Its walls are covered with protruding COPIED ARMS, each holding an item offered for trade. Every arm reproduces the seller's hand and remains active even while the seller is elsewhere in the living world.
- Buyers move physically through the space, inspecting the goods held out from the walls.
fields.rules:
##### Trade Mechanics
- Barter only, arm to arm. The planted arms throughout the market grab at any "suitable object" presented to them, dropping their own goods as they snatch.
- The exchange itself completes the sale. The buyer leaves with the purchased item, while the offered payment is delivered immediately into the seller's hand in the living world, regardless of where the seller has gone since registering the item.
- A seller does not need to remain beside the original manhole. Until the item is sold, their projected arm continues holding it inside the Market and reacts according to the desire fixed at the time of registration.
- Suitability is defined by each seller's DESIRE: an arm reaches for what its owner wants, and nothing else. Reading what a stall reaches for is reading its owner.
- Underlying hazard: the parent tale still eats people. The market is a use-case built on a predator, and sloppy access  reverts the relationship to the original menu.

##### Exit
- The manhole cover used for entry appears overhead at the visitor's point of arrival. To leave, the visitor must reach up and open that same cover. The moment it is lifted, the visitor and any goods obtained through completed trades are returned to the living world beside the original manhole.
- The return passage remains safe for one hour from the moment of entry. Once that limit is exceeded, the connection reverts to the parent tale: a Manhole Arm waits on the other side of the exit, and the visitor is no longer recognized as a customer.

fields.identity:
##### Registration and Status
- A anomaly disguised as a private counselling room. Provides counselling, trauma care, and mental / spiritual contamination recovery.
fields.access:
- Fox Counseling has no fixed entrance. It manifests when a wooden plaque reading "Fox Counseling" appears on an otherwise ordinary door.
- Opening the marked door no longer leads to the space normally connected to it. Instead, the doorway opens into the Counseling's changing room.
- The plaque may appear on doors in facilities, shelters, safehouses, clinics, private buildings, liminal spaces, or anomaly-adjacent locations.
- After the session, the client exits through the same door. The plaque disappears immediately, and opening the door again reveals the original space as though the Counseling had never been there.
fields.location:
##### Space and Procedure
- Entry area: Changing room with hospital-style gowns, green with grass patterns, organised by size. Must change into the provided gown before entering the counselling area.
- The room: warm sunlight through a window, a plush pastel-toned sofa, and a small silver bell as a door chime, clear-toned, deliberate. Only the client may enter the counselling space proper. Other people must wait in the changing room. 
- Posted instruction, in full: "Sit comfortably on the sofa and enjoy the view outside!" That is the entire procedure. The session begins when something arrives OUTSIDE the window to conduct it.
fields.rules:
##### Effect
- Meaningful recovery of mental stability and mild contamination. "It's amazing. It brought back the motivation I'd lost, and made me remember things I'd forgotten."
- Removal of cursed objects or anomalous influences embedded in the client's body, possessions, or psyche.
- For severe cases, offers red berries, tentatively identified as Fox Pouch / Fox Bead family, that dissolve pain when consumed.
- DO NOT agree to weekly or biweekly recurring sessions. This dramatically increases the risk of adverse side effects.
fields.keeper:
##### The Counselor
-  Takes forms tailored to each client's needs. Often manifests as the client, a trusted figure, an idealised self, or someone emotionally significant.
- Does not normally request money, goods, or favours.
- Highly perceptive and empathetic. The counselor perceives and acknowledges bonds invisible to normal observation.
- Appears benevolent under normal use but has documented cases of clients vanishing after agreeing to regular weekly / biweekly sessions.

fields.identity:
##### Origin
- An anomalous plush keyring doll distributed with an instruction manual. When the enclosed rite is performed correctly, the doll becomes an anchor for an external entity, allowing it to remain beside the summoner as a presence whose voice only the summoner can hear.
fields.access:
##### How to obtain
- Good Friend dolls occasionally appear in ordinary retail circulation without warning, mixed among legitimate toys or delivered through unidentified promotional channels. 
- The Bureau recognizes the dolls as potentially dangerous anomalous products and attempts to locate, recover, and destroy them before they can be used. Recovery remains incomplete, as new units continue to surface unpredictably.
fields.rules:
##### The Invitation Rite: enclosed instructions, full text
- Materials: one Good Friend doll, an open flame, 100 ml of water, one spoonful of salt, one clean coin, and an object connected to the entity being summoned
- Procedure:
1. With a water-dipped finger, draw the enclosed hexagram design on a smooth floor.
2. Place the Kind Friend at the hexagram's exact center.
3. Set a coin on the Kind Friend's belly. No water may remain on your fingers at this step.
4. Hold a spoonful of salt in your mouth, and burn an object connected to your friend.
5. When the Kind Friend begins to speak, swallow the salt and return the greeting warmly!
- Success condition: the coin has vanished. You have met a steadfast friend. Be together always, and cherish them.
- Failure Warning: If the salt cannot be swallowed, tastes strange, turns to ash, or causes bleeding, RUN.

##### Mechanism
- The burned object serves as the ADDRESS. It identifies a being connected to that object and gives the rite a target to call.
- The safety of the answer is exactly the reality of the friendship: the rite has no opinion about what your "friend" is, only about whether it is one. The warning clause exists because not everyone who calls has a friend on the other end, and something still answers.
- A successful connection gives the entity access to the doll as its vessel, voice, and anchor on this side.
fields.keeper:
##### The Summoned Entity
- The answering presence may be a higher-dimensional outsider wearing a familiar face, name, or persona, or an Anomaly possessing its own identity, history, and will.
- It arrives as a fully realized personage with its own memories, tastes, motives, voice, and manner.
- Its intellect may vastly exceed that of a human. It can converse, reason, persuade, and joke as fluently as any person.

extra.name: Forms
extra.value:
- A small plush keyring available in assorted animal designs.
- The package copy reads: "Your adorable animal doll. It will always go with you and protect you. Always." The second "always" is literal.

extra.name: Manifestation
extra.value:
- The doll retains its original soft plush keyring form regardless of which object was burned or which entity answers.
- The offering determines the entity being called, not the physical form of the doll.
- The entity remains on its own side and reaches through the doll, using it as an anchor in the living world.
- Its voice is heard only by the summoner, as though speaking directly within their mind. To everyone else, the doll remains still and silent.
- Its company takes the form of counsel, observation, and perspective carried through this private voice. 
- Beneath the agreeable surface may run something colder. a private agenda, an appetite, an amusement at summoner's expense, shown only in brief glints.

extra.name: Summons cases
extra.value:
- A rabbit keyring inhabited by the broadcaster-entity Brownie.
- A cat keyring inhabited by the cosmic outsider Nyarlathotep.

fields.identity:
- The Anything Vending Machine is a bright-red anomalous vending machine that appears in arbitrary locations and offers situation-specific items at the cost of body parts.
- It does not directly compel anyone to buy. Its danger lies in presenting something a prospective customer may need badly enough to accept the stated price.
fields.access:
- The machine manifests unpredictably in arbitrary locations, including alleys, building interiors, sealed rooms, and other spaces a vending machine could not physically enter.
- Anyone who encounters it may use it. Its inventory appears to adapt to the circumstances, desires, dangers, or fears of those nearby.
- The machine decides when to vanish, usually after a transaction, after the user leaves, or once its interest ends.
- The same individual may encounter it repeatedly, but this appears incidental rather than evidence that the machine selects or follows specific customers.
fields.location:
##### Appearance
- It resembles an ordinary bright-red vending machine with standard dimensions, buttons, a display window, and a mundane commercial design.
- Products may change between appearances or while being observed. Their labels are frequently pun-based, ominous, or tailored to the surrounding situation.
- Transactions are accompanied by cheerful jingles, congratulatory tones, and customer-service messages that remain grotesquely upbeat regardless of the price paid.
fields.rules:
##### Transaction
- The machine accepts body parts only. The price is roughly proportional to the item's value as judged by the machine, not necessarily by the customer.
- Each product displays the exact body part that will be collected before purchase. The person who presses the selection button becomes the purchaser and pays the displayed price.
- Pressing the button constitutes final consent. There is no cancellation, refund, negotiation, substitution, or appeal after selection.
- The selected item is dispensed first. Payment is collected immediately afterward by numerous black hands emerging from impossible directions and moving too quickly to evade.
- Collection is performed with surgical precision. The victim does not bleed to death from the removal itself unless the agreed price is inherently fatal.
- The machine fulfills the displayed transaction exactly, but only according to the literal terms shown. It makes no guarantee that the product is safe, complete, or beneficial.

##### Inventory and Services
- Despite its name, the machine does not provide anything requested on demand. Customers may choose only from the products it elects to display.
- Its inventory ranges from genuinely useful tools to viciously ironic products, such as a weapon suited to the current threat, an umbrella offered during drowning, or sunscreen offered in complete darkness.
- The items it provides may save the user, ruin them through cruel irony, or tempt them into paying far more than they realize.
- The inventory's constant adaptation suggests awareness of the customer's circumstances and a deliberate sense of dark humor or cruelty.
- Items frequently possess undisclosed properties that become apparent only when used. Their labels are usually accurate, but rarely comprehensive.

우주 쇼핑몰.keys: Space Shopping, Cosmos Shopping, 우주 쇼핑몰

fields.identity: - The Space Shopping Mall is a hidden commercial zone selling anomalous merchandise of unknown extraterrestrial origin. Anyone who finds an active storefront may enter.
fields.access:
##### Location and Access
- The Space Shopping Mall has no fixed address. Its entrance occasionally replaces a VACANT storefront inside an existing commercial building, marked by a spinning green UFO sign and the banner: <SPACE SHOPPING MALL> ※AWESOME GOODS FROM OUTER SPACE※.
- Opening the storefront door leads directly into the Mall, regardless of what space normally exists behind it.
- The entrance door remains visible from inside the Mall. Opening it returns the visitor to the commercial building through which they entered.
- Once manifested, the Mall remains open for approximately one day. The entrance then disappears, leaving the original vacant storefront behind as though nothing had occupied it.
fields.location:
##### Appearance
- The Mall resembles a small shopping arcade preserved from the early 2000s, with raw typefaces, underlined signs, cheap plastic fixtures, flickering fluorescent lights, and a spinning green UFO suspended above the entrance.
- The interior contains a shifting number of storefronts and display counters, but no employees or other visible operators. 
- A large sign near the entrance reads: "I will look at the goods."
fields.rules:
##### Inventory and Pricing
- The Mall sells outlandish anomalous merchandise at equally outlandish prices. Entry-level products begin at approximately one million won and increase without any apparent upper limit.
- Payment is accepted in ordinary CASH or by standard credit and debit cards. Each display has a marked price and an attached payment terminal.
- Once payment is approved, the corresponding display unlocks and the product may be removed. Card transactions appear on the purchaser's statement under inconsistent or untraceable merchant names.
- The Mall's inventory changes each time it opens. Products recorded during one appearance may be absent during the next, while entirely new items may replace them without notice.
- Recorded merchandise includes:
   - A fork-and-knife weapon set that absorbs blood and grows larger and sharper with continued use.
   - The Wider Walkie-Talkie, a toy radio capable of remote communication even from inside anomaly.
   - The Alice Picnic Set, containing a drink that doubles an object's effect and a cookie that halves it.
   - We Help!, an unexplained product priced beyond most practical budgets.
   - The Silver-Coin Snake, an anomalous product whose method of use remains unknown.
- Some products are occasionally offered ON SALE.

##### Nature and Risk
- All recorded products are genuine and perform according to their descriptions, though labels may omit limitations, side effects, or consequences.
- Theft, deliberate damage, or interference with the displays causes the offender to be immediately teleported to what is presumed to be the Mall's HEADQUARTERS. No one taken there has ever returned.

우주 쇼핑몰.title: Space Shopping Mall

fields.identity:
##### Overview
- A Twilight grade facility Uh-doom held in the Annex beside Baekilmong headquarters, and the Field Exploration Team's primary means of manufacturing custom equipment.
- The company does not run it as a hazard. It runs it as a factory, and charges its own employees for the privilege.
fields.access:
##### Containment and Access
- The Annex ground floor leads down to a dim basement reception desk staffed by a silent figure dressed head to toe in black, with mask, sunglasses, and hat. Visitors state their squad and the darkness number.
- On approval the figure nods once and opens one of the emergency doors behind the desk, revealing a corridor lined with countless numbered doors. Standing rule among employees: never open any other room, and do not even touch the handles.
- Door 99 opens onto a greenhouse choked with weeds under pouring moonlight, and at its exact center stands one huge rusted machine. Every weed in the greenhouse is artificial, and a sensor at the door filters out real plants.
fields.keeper:
##### The Machine
- Power source: moonlight. The kit only operates on a moonlit night.
- Interface: an aged LCD screen with quaint lettering. Idle prompt: "Please give me a plant 0/2". On scanning an item: "Plant information saved", then the counter advances to 1/2.
- Usage fee: 1,000p per run, paid because Annex Twilight darknesses only operate when the fee is paid. Employees at Joo-im rank and above receive two free runs per year, so the standing culture is to wait for promotion, which usually takes about a year of survival.
- Squad custom: when a member makes their FIRST custom equipment, someone in the squad lends their own equipment once, free of charge, as one of the two inputs. One slot only. The other slot is the maker's own object.
fields.rules:
##### Crafting Procedure
- Step 1, first parent: hold the first item against the machine so it can scan the item's "genetic information". The screen reads "Plant information saved", then "Please give me a plant 1/2".
- Step 2, second parent: scan the second item the same way. The screen advances to "Please give me a plant 2/2".
- Step 3, gardener registration: the screen reads "Please tell me the gardener's information". The maker scans themselves. The machine demands the genetic information of the guardian who will tend the new plant, and this registers ownership. The gardener's information also acts as a variable in what the seed becomes.
- Step 4, sowing: the screen reads "Confirmed", then "Combining genetic information", then "Generating kit....". Five-colored smoke vents from the machine and gears grind and creak inside.
- Step 5, harvest: the screen reads "Sowing complete". A drawer at the front of the machine slides open holding a single new object.
- The parent items are NOT consumed. Both are scanned only, and their owners take them back on the spot. This is why lending a parent item costs the lender nothing but the trip.
- The output usually takes the everyday form of one of its parents, and its ability may be entirely latent and undocumented. The maker discovers the activation method themselves, by trial, usually somewhere safe.
- Company-side record of the result: owner, registered equipment description, manufactured at Qterw-E-99.

##### Crafting and Inheritance Rules
- It is a machine that treats OBJECTS as PLANTS: feed it two items and it reads their "genetic information", crossbreeds the two, and sows one new object that inherits their traits. 
- Trait synergy between the two parents matters. The better the source, the better the result.
- An ordinary convenient object in the second slot may inherit the supernatural trait WEAKLY, or, with low probability, not at all. The machine offers no refund for a dud.

##### The Plant Prohibition
- A sign fixed to the machine reads: ABSOLUTELY NO PLANTS. No matter how the screen asks, never feed it a real plant.
- Crafting record #14: an employee tore up weeds growing near the darkness, presumed dandelion, and fed the machine twice. The output emerged screaming. All three people on site died, suppression by the Guard Team took seven days.

extra.name: Known Products
extra.value:
- The Third Hand: a coin-shaped device that summons an extra hand in midair.
- Tricolor ballpoint: a pen whose tip, when clicked, fires off and bursts like a firecracker.
- Chainless handcuffs: an invisible cuff chain that keeps two wearers within a set radius of one another.
- Strength bracelet: a braided bracelet resembling woven human hair, granting enhanced physical power.

이빨 요정.keys: Tooth Tree, 이빨 나무, 이빨 요정

fields.identity:
- A linked pair of specimens contained in separate sealed cells in the Bureau's deepest underground Containment Team sector.
- Tooth Tree: A thick, trunk-like pillar in an unlit cell of roughly ten pyeong, densely covered with human molar-like teeth. Unless regularly harvested, the teeth multiply until they fill the room. Handlers use an extraction rig stored in the cell cabinet to pull them and load them into boxes. Each emptied socket bleeds before slowly growing a replacement. All harvested teeth are used to feed the Tooth Fairy.
- Tooth Fairy: A swarm of forearm-sized creatures, each with a lamprey-like head, an earthworm-shaped body, two thin human-like arms, and dragonfly-like wings. Handlers scatter teeth harvested from the Tooth Tree across the cell floor. After feeding, the largest individual produces a neatly wrapped box from an unknown source. The box is larger than the creature itself and roughly the size and weight of a basketball; one observed example was pink with a green ribbon.
- The Gift Box: Every box is sealed inside the cell and transferred to the Containment Team laboratory, where its contents are examined with a laser-scanning rig before opening. The contents appear random and are often difficult to identify. The most valuable results are organs or bones previously taken from agents by other anomalies. Personnel missing irreplaceable body parts may therefore be frozen and preserved in the hope that the missing part will eventually be returned. Worthless contents, including stray animal bone fragments, are logged as duds and discarded.
- Handling Protocol:
   1. Supply teeth on a regular schedule.
   2. Wear a full protective suit, leaving no skin or nails exposed.
   3. Keep the mouth closed at all times and communicate only through sign language inside the cell.
   4. Do not remove any Tooth Fairy from the cell.
   5. Do not investigate the origin or production of a gift box without permission from the Containment Team laboratory.
   6. Seal every received box and deliver it directly to the laboratory.
   7. Treat the presentation of a box as conditioned behavior, not gratitude. Personnel who develop emotional attachment must report immediately to the Bureau psychiatric team.
   8. Anyone with prior professional experience as a dentist is prohibited from entering the cell.

이빨 요정.title: Tooth Tree & Tooth Fairy

망상홈쇼핑.keys: Delusion Home Shopping, 망상홈쇼핑, 망상 홈쇼핑, Red Friday, 레드 프라이데이, 망상 홈쇼핑 라이브

fields.identity:
- A 24-hour 2000s-style TV shopping channel selling anomalous merchandise whose advertised effects are real; that is the danger.
- A platform, not a maker: it sources items from other Uh-doom, anomalous workshops, and dead sellers' stock and markets them to whatever demand exists, often for a purpose other than the one they were made for. The original purpose survives under the label.
- Once a bizarre ad that cut into ordinary TV unannounced on Friday nights; since the Day of Disaster the permanent tenant of Blood Broadcasting Station at Segwang's Afternoon Station (see 오후역 for the studio). Broadcasts, app, and deliveries reach far beyond Segwang.
fields.access:
##### Contact
- Friday Interruption: on Friday nights any screen left on can switch to the channel; changing channels brings it back one channel later. Switching off works, but the host's voice runs on a few seconds after the screen goes black.
- Live App: "Delusion Home Shopping Live" installs itself and appoints the owner as audience; deleted, it often returns next Friday. Chat mixes shopping talk with pleas ("Delivery time?" / "I'm in here" / "Restock on item 2?" / "Anyone know the way out").
- Staff Contracts: posters of smiling models injuring themselves lead to an intake room with a pen and a one-day contract for "unspecified support duties, performance-based pay." Signing makes the signer staff.
- Stray Goods: boxes with the channel's sticker, usage instructions, and air date (e.g., "aired June 1, 19XX") turn up in pharmacies, gyms, clinics, flea markets, stockrooms. Baekilmong has bought whole lots for experiments.
fields.rules:
##### Studio Audience
- On air and in the app a banner offers "Studio audience wanted! Free seats, free gifts, special audience prices" with a number or button. Applicants are pulled, with whatever they hold, into the Main Studio seats at the next broadcast; anyone touching them comes along as their guest.
- Each gets a numbered paddle and lanyard pass. Audience is a guest status, separate from staff and demonstration models; lose paddle and pass and only those two categories remain.
- Rules, read by a floor manager before airtime: applaud and laugh on the cue lights (silence or visible fear draws the camera); never cross the floor tape; when the host asks "Who in our audience would like to try it?", do not raise a hand, stand, or meet his eyes (volunteers become models); touch nothing on the stage or demo table; stay seated until the credits roll and the EXIT sign over the audience door lights, then leave only by that door, which returns each person to where they applied.
- In commercial breaks a runner leads the audience behind the bleachers to a glass-cased showroom of current and back-catalog stock, each case with price card, usage sticker, and sample. Samples may be examined freely; opening a case without a runner counts as buying.
- Haggle with runners, or with Red Friday in the "audience special" segment; he enjoys a good haggle on air and hates looking cheap. Audience prices beat phone prices.
- Payment: "interest-free installments," each an obligation to appear later as a model, extra, or caller; or a trade in anomalous items, Uh-doom material, or contracts, since this is how the channel sources stock. It underpays for anything whose purpose it reads better than the seller. Purchases come in a gift bag at the exit door; taking it accepts the sale.

##### Phone Orders
- Calling the on-screen number mid-segment reaches a polite operator; the order is real and ships in an ordinary courier box, often addressed to someone else. Whoever opens it accepts the purchase.
- Installments as above. Missed ones are collected by summoning the buyer onto the set unannounced, usually on a Friday. Contracts are channel property and can be sold or transferred.
- Confetti picked up near the studio can unfold into an order form with the picker's name in the quantity box; treat stray confetti, flyers, and slips as contracts. No refunds; returns are "processed" by demonstrating the item on air.

##### Merchandise
- The catalog is open-ended and changes by program, season, and demand. Each product has a cheerful ad, a real effect, strict usage instructions, and a hidden original purpose shown by embossing, foreign script, or a layer under the sticker. Following instructions exactly gives only the advertised effect; breaking them or adding a forbidden variable releases the original purpose. Demonstrations are real and often end in mutilation, parasitism, overdose, or death.

##### Survival Notes
- Order, sign, or pick up nothing from the channel unless that obligation is the goal; the least risky way to shop is as audience, keeping that status until the EXIT sign lights.
- Turn screens off when the channel appears on Friday nights. Do not keep watching any feed of Segwang City Hall's rooftop; covering the screen stops the humming it induces.
- Once chosen for a demonstration, the body follows the script to the end.
- Contracts are assets: buying, winning, or transferring the paperwork changes who owns a worker or buyer without defeating the channel.
- Keep stray merchandise sealed; if it must be used, follow the sticker exactly and find the hidden purpose first.

##### Personnel
- Red Friday, lead host: male-presenting, late thirties, black suit, groomed hair, unnaturally white makeup, huge black fully dilated eyes. On air smooth and relentless ("Customers, you will never see this price again. Call right now. See our model's face? That is the real effect!"); off air his mouth opens too far onto a bottomless scarlet throat. Politely bureaucratic toward other anomalies, indifferent to worker deaths. He stammers only when the landlord's rent call cuts in, then calls up another model; broadcasts grow harsher near rent day.
- Other hosts, runners, and staff share the white face, wide smile, and scarlet throat. Dead contract workers keep working, stiff but visibly frightened. Silent stagehands clear bodies and reset props. Callers are hauntings, dying screams, or nonhuman speech; hosts keep phone etiquette throughout.
